summary: Prince William County, VA CCC Camp P-71 steel tower, built 1934; dismantled and sold in 1988; site is now a volunteer fire station, with a 2014 marker.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a glass-enclosed platform, built for CCC Camp P-71 (Camp Recovery)

staffing.status: manned by watchmen; later used by local fire departments

facts.status_note: Dismantled and sold in 1988; no tower remains on the site, which is now a volunteer fire station

access.note: The tower site is now the grounds of the Coles District Volunteer Fire and Rescue station; the county marker stands on Dumfries Road. No source describes public access to the station grounds.

events.note: First enrollees of CCC Camp P-71 (Camp Recovery) arrived 15 October 1933
Register gives 1934; a photograph taken from the camp's fire tower dates to around February 1934
Disassembled and sold per register; dismantled in 1988; in South Carolina as of the reliquary's January 2008 issue
Historical marker erected by Prince William County Historical Commission

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1934 as the build year; the marker dates the camp's first enrollees to 15 October 1933. Not a real conflict: the story uses 1934 for the tower and gives the 1933 camp start separately.

Reliquary places the tower just south of the present fire station, and says the property is where the station stands. The marker is on Dumfries Road about 0.1 miles north of Hoadly Road. The story says the station sits just north of where the tower stood.

notes_for_editor: Three independent sources agree on the 1988 removal and that the site is now a fire station. Staffing is one local recollection in the reliquary (names of the Ellicott brothers); the story keeps it general. Record coordinates (38.6586, -77.4405) sit about 130 m from the marker's listed point (38.65975, -77.44063); no correction proposed. The register names the volunteer fire department as administrator; the marker says the Virginia Forest Service supervised fire control at the camp.
